12-1.bio:
The holy prophet Nahum is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament. He prophesied the fall of Nineveh, the proud capital of Assyria, declaring that the Lord is slow to anger and great in power, a stronghold in the day of trouble to those who trust in Him, and that the oppressor's city would not rise again.

The Church honors him among the prophets whose words prepared Israel for the justice and mercy of God revealed in Christ. He is commemorated on December 1.
12-1.name: Nahum the Prophet

12-1.bio:
Righteous Philaret lived in the eighth century at Amnia in Paphlagonia, a wealthy landowner who gave to every needy person who came to his door until he had reduced his own household to poverty. His wife and children reproached him, but he continued to give away even his last ox and his last measure of grain, trusting in God.

Tradition relates that his granddaughter Maria was chosen as bride for the emperor Constantine VI, and that Philaret used the honours that followed only to feed the poor of Constantinople, where he reposed in peace.
12-1.desc: Righteous Philaret the Merciful of Amnia in Paphlagonia, famed for his boundless almsgiving.
12-1.name: Philaret the Merciful

12-1.bio:
The holy martyr Ananias suffered for Christ in Persia. Brought before the pagan authorities and commanded to worship the sun and fire, he confessed Christ and was cruelly beaten and tormented.

Tradition relates that he was strengthened by a heavenly vision in the midst of his sufferings and so gave up his soul to God.
12-1.name: Ananias the Persian

12-1.bio: Onesimus was Archbishop of Ephesus, one of the ancient apostolic sees of Asia Minor. The Synaxarion records that he shepherded his flock in holiness and reposed in peace; the Church also remembers on this day his fellow hierarchs of Ephesus, Ananias and Solochon.
12-1.desc: Onesimus, Archbishop of Ephesus, who reposed in peace.
12-1.name: Onesimus of Ephesus

12-1.bio: Theokletos was Archbishop of Lacedaemonia in the Peloponnese, remembered by the Church as a wonderworker. Tradition places him in the Byzantine period and relates that he shepherded the people of the region of Sparta with pastoral zeal, working miracles both in his lifetime and after his repose. He is honoured as a patron of the Church of Sparta and Monemvasia.
12-1.desc: Theokletos the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Lacedaemonia (Sparta).
12-1.name: Theokletos of Lacedaemonia

12-1.bio: Venerable Antony the New is an ascetic of the Byzantine period commemorated by the Greek Synaxarion on this day. Tradition relates that he held office in the world before renouncing it for the monastic life, and that he lived in obedience and stillness until his peaceful repose.
12-1.name: Antony the New

12-10.bio:
The holy martyrs Menas, Hermogenes, and Eugraphus suffered at Alexandria in the early fourth century. Menas, called the Melodious for his eloquence, was sent to the city on imperial business and openly preached Christ there; Hermogenes, sent to judge him, was won to the faith by his endurance and the grace shown in him, and Eugraphus, the companion of Menas, confessed Christ with them. All three were put to death by beheading.

The Church honors them as witnesses whose wisdom and courage turned even their persecutor to Christ. They are commemorated on December 10.
12-10.desc: Holy Martyrs Menas, Hermogenes and Eugraphus.
12-10.name: Menas, Hermogenes and Eugraphus

12-10.bio: Venerable Thomas was a monk of Bithynia in the tenth century who lived for many years in solitude near the monastery of Defourkinos. Tradition relates that the emperor Leo the Wise sent him a sealed letter with questions, and that the saint answered them without opening the seal, so great was his gift of discernment.
12-10.name: Thomas of Bithynia

12-10.bio: The holy martyr Gemellus was a Christian of Paphlagonia who openly rebuked the emperor Julian the Apostate at Ancyra. Tradition relates that he was tortured and finally crucified for Christ, ending his life on the cross like his Master.
12-10.desc: Holy Martyr Gemellus of Paphlagonia, crucified under Julian the Apostate.
12-10.name: Gemellus of Paphlagonia

12-10.bio: The holy martyrs Theotecnus, Marianus and Eugene are commemorated together on this day. The Synaxarion records that they confessed Christ and were perfected by the sword.
12-10.desc: Holy Martyrs Theotecnus, Marianus and Eugene.
12-10.name: Theotecnus, Marianus and Eugene

12-10.bio: Athanasius was born in Catania in Sicily in the ninth century and, when his family fled the Arab invasions to the Peloponnese, he became a monk at Patras and was later made Bishop of Methoni. He shepherded his flock in humility and reposed in peace.
12-10.desc: Athanasius, Bishop of Methoni in the Peloponnese.
12-10.name: Athanasius of Methoni

12-11.bio:
Venerable Daniel the Stylite was a monk of the fifth century who, inspired by the example of St. Symeon the Stylite, took his stand upon a pillar near Constantinople and remained there in prayer for more than thirty years, enduring frost, wind, and burning heat. Emperors and patriarchs climbed to seek his counsel, and he came down only once, to defend the Orthodox faith in the capital.

He reposed in extreme old age, revered by the whole city as an intercessor and guide. He is commemorated on December 11.
12-11.name: Daniel the Stylite

12-11.bio: Venerable Luke was a soldier who became a monk and priest in the tenth century. He took his stand upon a pillar near Chalcedon, where he lived in prayer and fasting for more than forty years, drawing many to repentance. He reposed in peace in the tenth century.
12-11.desc: Venerable Luke the New Stylite of Chalcedon.
12-11.name: Luke the New Stylite

12-11.bio: The holy martyr Mirax was an Egyptian Christian who in his youth denied Christ and embraced the religion of the conquerors. Moved by the tears and prayers of his parents, he repented, openly confessed Christ before the ruler, and was beheaded. His story is told in the Synaxarion as an example of the power of repentance.
12-11.desc: Holy Martyr Mirax of Egypt, who returned to Christ after denying Him.
12-11.name: Mirax of Egypt

12-11.bio: The holy martyrs Aithalas and Akepsimas are remembered together on this day. The Synaxarion records that they confessed Christ and were perfected by the sword; the Church also remembers on this day the martyrs Terence, Vincent, Aemilianus and Bebaia.
12-11.name: Aithalas and Akepsimas

12-11.bio: Venerable Leontios was born in Monemvasia and became a monk on Mount Athos before withdrawing to a cave on the mountains of Achaia near Aigio, where he lived in stillness and prayer. He reposed in peace in the fifteenth century and is honoured at the monastery of the Taxiarchs there.
12-11.name: Leontios of Achaia

12-11.bio: Nikephoros Phokas was a Byzantine general who recovered Crete from the Arabs and reigned as emperor from 963. A friend of St. Athanasios the Athonite, he supported the founding of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos and lived with monastic austerity in the palace. He was murdered in 969 and is remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day.
12-11.desc: Righteous Emperor Nikephoros Phokas, benefactor of the Great Lavra of Athos.
12-11.name: Nikephoros Phokas

12-11.bio: On this day the Church of Georgia gathers in one commemoration all the saints of its land, from St. Nina, Equal to the Apostles, and the early martyrs to the monastic fathers and the confessors of later centuries. The synaxis is also kept in the Greek calendar.
12-11.desc: Synaxis of all the Saints who have shone forth in the land of Georgia.
12-11.name: Synaxis of All Saints of Georgia

12-12.bio:
St. Spyridon, Bishop of Trimythous in Cyprus, was a shepherd of great simplicity and holiness who lived in the fourth century. Married and later widowed, he was made bishop while continuing to tend his sheep. According to tradition, at the First Ecumenical Council he demonstrated the unity of the Holy Trinity by pressing a clay tile, from which fire rose, water flowed, and earth remained in his hand.

His incorrupt relics rest on Corfu, whose patron he is, and many miracles are ascribed to his intercession through the centuries. He is commemorated on December 12 and honored with processions on Corfu several times each year.
12-12.desc: Bishop Spyridon of Tremithus, wonderworker, patron of Corfu.
12-12.name: Spyridon of Trimythous

12-12.bio: Venerable John was Bishop of Zichna in Macedonia in the fourteenth century. Together with his uncle Joachim he founded and built up the monastery of the Honourable Forerunner near Serres, which became one of the great monastic centres of northern Greece. He reposed in peace there.
12-12.desc: Venerable John, Bishop of Zichna, founder of the Monastery of the Forerunner near Serres.
12-12.name: John of Zichna

12-12.bio: The hieromartyr Alexander was a pupil of Clement of Alexandria and a friend of Origen. Bishop first in Cappadocia, he was chosen to share the see of Jerusalem, where he founded a library and a school. In the persecution of Decius he confessed Christ and died in prison at Caesarea in the middle of the third century.
12-12.name: Alexander of Jerusalem

12-12.bio: The holy martyr Synetus was a reader of the Church of Rome in the third century. Brought before the emperor Aurelian, he confessed Christ boldly and was beheaded.
12-12.desc: Holy Martyr Synetus, reader of the Church of Rome.
12-12.name: Synetus of Rome

12-12.bio: Venerable Therapon was a Russian monk of the sixteenth century who founded a monastery on the river Monza in the Kostroma region. Known for his humility and gift of prophecy, he reposed in peace in 1597.
12-12.desc: Venerable Therapon, abbot of the Monastery of Monza in Russia.
12-12.name: Therapon of Monza

12-13.bio:
The holy Five Martyrs Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugene, Mardarius, and Orestes suffered for Christ in Armenia during the persecution under Diocletian at the turn of the fourth century. Eustratius, a distinguished imperial officer, confessed Christ openly and endured many torments together with his companions, each of whom sealed his faith with his blood.

The prayer of St. Eustratius, spoken before his death, is read in the Church's midnight service to this day. They are commemorated on December 13.
12-13.name: Eustratius and companions

12-13.bio:
The holy virgin martyr Lucy was a Christian of Syracuse in Sicily who suffered under the persecution of Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. Having vowed her virginity to Christ and given her dowry to the poor, she was denounced by her suitor and brought before the governor.

Tradition relates that no force could move her from where she stood, and that she was finally slain by the sword. She is honoured throughout East and West.
12-13.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Lucy of Syracuse.
12-13.name: Lucy of Syracuse

12-13.bio: Venerable Arsenios was a Byzantine official who became a monk on Mount Latros near Miletus, where he was later chosen abbot of the monastery of Kellibara. Tradition relates that he was a wonderworker who reposed in peace.
12-13.desc: Venerable Arsenios, ascetic of Mount Latros.
12-13.name: Arsenios of Latros

12-13.bio: The hieromartyr Gabriel was Patriarch of the Serbs at Pec in the seventeenth century. Accused before the Ottoman authorities on his return from Russia, he refused to embrace Islam and was hanged at Bursa in 1659.
12-13.desc: Hieromartyr Gabriel, Patriarch of Pec and Archbishop of Serbia.
12-13.name: Gabriel of Pec

12-13.bio:
Venerable Herman was a monk of Valaam who came to Alaska with the first Orthodox mission in 1794. He lived for decades on Spruce Island, caring for the native Aleuts, defending them against injustice, and teaching the children; he reposed there in 1837.

The Greek Synaxarion remembers on this day the hieromonk Juvenal and Peter the Aleut and all the saints who have shone forth in Alaska.
12-13.desc: Venerable Herman of Alaska and all the Saints of Alaska.
12-13.name: Herman of Alaska

12-13.bio: These venerable fathers of the twelfth century founded the monastery of the Theotokos of Machairas in the mountains of Cyprus, around an icon of the Mother of God found there according to tradition. Neilos, the third of the founders, was later made Bishop of Tamassos. They are honoured as patrons of one of the great monasteries of Cyprus.
12-13.desc: Venerable Neophytos, Ignatios, Prokopios and Neilos, founders of the Monastery of Machairas in Cyprus.
12-13.name: Founders of Machairas Monastery

12-14.bio:
The holy martyrs Thyrsos, Leucius, and Callinicus suffered for Christ in Asia Minor in the third century, during the Roman persecutions. Refusing to offer sacrifice to the idols, they endured torments with steadfast faith and were put to death, their endurance drawing others to confess Christ.

The synaxaria preserve little beyond their faithful witness, which the Church holds in honor among the martyrs of that age. They are commemorated on December 14.
12-14.desc: Holy Martyrs Thyrsus, Leucius, and Callinicus.
12-14.name: Thyrsos and companions

12-14.bio: These holy martyrs suffered at Antinoe in Egypt under Diocletian. Philemon, a pagan flute-player, was converted when he took the place of the Christian Apollonius before the governor Arrian; both were put to death. Tradition relates that Arrian himself later believed and was martyred together with four of his bodyguards, the Protectors.
12-14.desc: Holy Martyrs Philemon, Apollonius, Arrian and the four Protectors, at Antinoe in Egypt.
12-14.name: Philemon, Apollonius and Arrian

12-14.bio: The holy martyr Hypatius and thirty-six companions are remembered together on this day. The Synaxarion records that they confessed Christ and were perfected by the sword.
12-14.desc: Holy Martyr Hypatius and the thirty-six martyrs who suffered with him.
12-14.name: Hypatius and the Thirty-Six Martyrs

12-15.bio:
The holy hieromartyr Eleutherios was a bishop of the early Church, raised in piety by his mother Anthia and consecrated to the episcopate while still young. According to tradition he suffered in the persecutions of the second century: brought before the emperor, he refused to deny Christ, endured many torments unharmed, and was finally put to death, his mother Anthia being slain beside him.

His name means freedom, and the faithful ask his intercession for deliverance from every bond; his feast is a beloved name day for Eleftherios and Lefteris. He is commemorated on December 15.
12-15.name: Eleutherios

12-15.bio: The holy martyr Anthia was the mother of the hieromartyr Eleutherios, whom she raised in the faith from childhood. When her son was put to death, she embraced his body and was herself beheaded, sharing his crown of martyrdom.
12-15.desc: Holy Martyr Anthia, mother of the Hieromartyr Eleutherios.
12-15.name: Anthia the Martyr

12-15.bio:
The venerable martyr Susanna was the daughter of a pagan priest in Palestine who came to faith in Christ. Tradition relates that she disguised herself as a man and entered a monastery, where she was falsely accused; when her innocence was revealed she was made a deaconess at Eleutheropolis.

In the persecution of Maximian she confessed Christ and was martyred.
12-15.desc: Venerable Martyr Susanna the Deaconess of Palestine.
12-15.name: Susanna the Deaconess

12-15.bio: Venerable Paul was born in Bithynia in the tenth century and became a monk on Mount Latros near Miletus, living in caves and on the summit of the mountain in great austerity. Many disciples gathered around him, and he was consulted by emperors. He reposed in peace in 955.
12-15.desc: Venerable Paul the New, ascetic of Mount Latros.
12-15.name: Paul of Latros

12-15.bio: The holy martyr Bacchus was born in Palestine in the eighth century to a father who had abandoned the Christian faith. Baptised and made a monk at the Lavra of St. Sabas, he was denounced as an apostate from Islam and beheaded in Jerusalem.
12-15.desc: Holy Martyr Bacchus the New of Palestine.
12-15.name: Bacchus the New

12-15.bio: Stephen was Archbishop of Sourozh in Crimea in the eighth century. He confessed the veneration of the holy icons against the iconoclast emperors, suffered imprisonment and exile, and returned to his see, where he reposed in peace.
12-15.desc: Stephen the Confessor, Archbishop of Sourozh in Crimea.
12-15.name: Stephen of Sourozh

12-15.bio: The holy martyr Eleutherios was a chamberlain of the imperial court. Tradition relates that he was denounced as a Christian by a servant, refused to deny Christ, and was beheaded.
12-15.desc: Holy Martyr Eleutherios the Cubicularius of Constantinople.
12-15.name: Eleutherios the Cubicularius

12-16.bio:
The holy prophet Aggaeus, called Haggai in the Hebrew Scriptures, is one of the twelve minor prophets. He prophesied in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian captivity, stirring up the people and their leaders to rebuild the Temple of the Lord, and declaring that the glory of the latter house would surpass the former.

The Church honors him among the prophets whose words looked beyond the earthly Temple to the coming of Christ. He is commemorated on December 16.
12-16.name: Aggaeus the Prophet

12-16.bio:
Holy Theophano was the first wife of the emperor Leo the Wise in the ninth century. Amid the splendour and the sorrows of the palace she lived in prayer, fasting and almsgiving, sleeping on the floor and giving her wealth to the poor.

She reposed in peace while still young, and her relics in Constantinople became a source of healing.
12-16.desc: Holy Empress Theophano the Wonderworker, wife of Emperor Leo the Wise.
12-16.name: Theophano the Empress

12-16.bio:
Modestos was Archbishop of Jerusalem in the seventh century. After the Persians sacked the city and carried off the Holy Cross, he laboured to restore the ruined churches and monasteries of the Holy Land, and was formally made patriarch when the Cross was returned.

In Greek tradition he is invoked for the health of animals and livestock. He reposed in peace.
12-16.desc: Modestos, Archbishop of Jerusalem, patron of animals.
12-16.name: Modestos of Jerusalem

12-16.bio: The holy martyr Marinus was a Roman of noble family who confessed Christ in the third century. Tradition relates that he was tortured and beheaded for refusing to sacrifice to the idols.
12-16.name: Marinus of Rome

12-16.bio: Memnon was Archbishop of Ephesus, remembered in the Synaxarion as a hierarch who governed his church in piety and reposed in peace. The Church also remembers on this day the martyrs Probus and Hilary.
12-16.name: Memnon of Ephesus

12-16.bio: Nicholas Chrysoberges was Patriarch of Constantinople in the late tenth century, in the days of the emperor Basil II. He governed the Church with wisdom and reposed in peace in 991.
12-16.desc: Nicholas II Chrysoberges, Patriarch of Constantinople.
12-16.name: Nicholas Chrysoberges

12-17.bio:
The holy prophet Daniel was carried as a youth into the Babylonian captivity, where he served in the courts of kings without ever compromising his faith. God gave him understanding of dreams and visions of the kingdoms of the world and of the Son of Man; cast into the den of lions for praying to his God, he was preserved unharmed. With him the Church honors the Three Holy Youths, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, who walked unburned in the fiery furnace rather than worship the golden idol.

Their deliverance is sung in the Church as a figure of the Resurrection and of the Virgin Birth. They are commemorated on December 17.
12-17.desc: Holy Prophet Daniel and the Three Holy Youths Ananias, Azarias, Misael.
12-17.name: Daniel the Prophet

12-17.bio:
Dionysios was born on Zakynthos in 1547 to a noble family and became a monk on the Strofades islands. Made Archbishop of Aegina, he soon resigned his see and returned to his island, where he lived in humility at the monastery of the Theotokos at Anafonitria.

He is remembered above all for forgiving and sheltering the man who had killed his own brother. He reposed in 1622, and his incorrupt relics are venerated in Zakynthos, whose patron he is.
12-17.desc: Dionysios the New, Archbishop of Aegina, patron of Zakynthos.
12-17.name: Dionysios of Zakynthos

12-17.bio: The venerable Patermuthius and Copres were monks of Egypt who confessed Christ before Julian the Apostate. Tradition relates that Copres wavered for a moment and was restored by the prayers of Patermuthius, and that the soldier Alexander, seeing their steadfastness, believed. All three were put to death.
12-17.desc: Venerable Martyrs Patermuthius and Copres, and the Martyr Alexander, in Egypt.
12-17.name: Patermuthius, Copres and Alexander

12-17.bio: Venerable Stephen, whose name before his tonsure was Dunale, was a nobleman of the West who left all and became a monk. Tradition relates that he travelled to the holy places and to Egypt, where he confessed Christ before the Muslim ruler and endured suffering for the faith before his repose.
12-17.desc: Venerable Stephen the Confessor, formerly called Dunale.
12-17.name: Stephen the Confessor

12-18.bio:
The holy martyr Sebastian was a Roman soldier of high rank who suffered under the persecution of Diocletian at the end of the third century. A secret Christian who strengthened imprisoned confessors, he was denounced, bound to a tree, and shot with arrows; found still living, he confessed Christ again before the emperor and was then put to death. A company of martyrs who suffered with him is honored alongside him.

He is one of the most venerated of the Roman martyrs, in both East and West. He is commemorated on December 18.
12-18.name: Sebastian

12-18.bio: These holy martyrs were companions of St. Sebastian at Rome in the persecution of Diocletian. Many of them, including the prison-keeper Nikostratos and his wife Zoe, came to faith through Sebastian's preaching and the healing of Zoe, who had been mute. They confessed Christ and were put to death in various ways, sharing the martyr's crown.
12-18.desc: Holy Martyrs Nikostratos, Zoe, Tranquillinus, Marcia, Castorius, Claudius, Tiburtius, Castulus, Marcellinus and Mark, who suffered with Saint Sebastian.
12-18.greek: Νικόστρατος, Ζωή, Τραγκυλίνος και οι συν αυτοίς
12-18.name: Companions of Sebastian

12-18.bio: Holy Sophia is remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day as a wonderworker. Tradition records that she lived in holiness and reposed in peace.
12-18.name: Sophia the Wonderworker

12-18.bio:
Venerable Michael was born in Jerusalem in the eighth century and became a monk and later synkellos of the Patriarch of Jerusalem. Sent to Constantinople, he confessed the veneration of the holy icons before the iconoclast emperors and endured prison and exile.

After the restoration of the icons he was made abbot of the monastery of Chora, where he reposed in peace in 846.
12-18.desc: Venerable Michael the Synkellos, Confessor, of Jerusalem and Constantinople.
12-18.name: Michael the Synkellos

12-18.bio: Florus was Bishop of Amisus in Pontus. The Synaxarion records that he had served as a court official before embracing the monastic life, and that he governed his church in holiness and reposed in peace.
12-18.desc: Florus, Bishop of Amisus on the Black Sea.
12-18.name: Florus of Amisus

12-18.bio: The holy martyrs Zacchaeus, a deacon of Gadara, and Alphaeus, a reader of the church of Caesarea, suffered at Caesarea in Palestine at the beginning of the persecution of Diocletian. Their martyrdom is recorded by Eusebius, who tells that they were tortured and beheaded together.
12-18.desc: Holy Martyrs Zacchaeus the Deacon and Alphaeus the Reader, at Caesarea in Palestine.
12-18.greek: Ζακχαίος ο Διάκονος και Αλφειός ο Αναγνώστης
12-18.name: Zacchaeus and Alphaeus

12-18.bio: Venerable Daniel was a hermit of Moldavia in the fifteenth century who lived in a cell carved into the rock near the future monastery of Voronet. Tradition relates that he was the spiritual counsellor of the prince Stephen the Great, who built the monastery at his encouragement. He reposed in peace and is honoured by the Church of Romania.
12-18.desc: Venerable Daniel the Hesychast of Voronet in Moldavia.
12-18.name: Daniel the Hesychast

12-19.bio:
The holy martyr Boniface was a servant of a wealthy Roman woman, Aglais, in the early fourth century. Sent by her to the East to bring back relics of the martyrs, he watched the sufferings of the confessors at Tarsus, was pierced with compunction for his own careless life, and openly declared himself a Christian; he was tortured and beheaded, and his own relics were carried back to Rome, where Aglais received them and thereafter lived in repentance.

His story is treasured as an image of sudden, wholehearted repentance crowned by martyrdom. He is commemorated on December 19.
12-19.name: Boniface

12-19.bio:
Righteous Aglaia was a wealthy Roman noblewoman of the early fourth century. Having sent her servant Boniface to the East to bring back relics of the martyrs, she received instead his own body, for he had confessed Christ and been martyred at Tarsus.

She built a church for his relics, gave away her wealth, and spent the rest of her life in repentance and prayer, reposing in peace.
12-19.desc: Righteous Aglaia of Rome, who received the relics of the Martyr Boniface.
12-19.name: Aglaia of Rome

12-19.bio: The holy martyrs Elias, Probus and Ares were Egyptian Christians who were arrested on their way to visit the confessors in Cilicia. Brought before the governor at Ascalon, they confessed Christ and were put to death in the early fourth century.
12-19.desc: Holy Martyrs Elias, Probus and Ares, Egyptians who suffered at Ascalon.
12-19.name: Elias, Probus and Ares

12-19.bio: The holy martyrs Timothy and Polyeuctus are remembered together on this day. The Synaxarion records that they confessed Christ and were perfected by fire.
12-19.name: Timothy and Polyeuctus

12-19.bio: The holy martyrs Eutychius and Thessalonica, together with two hundred men and seventy women, are commemorated on this day. The Synaxarion records that they confessed Christ and were perfected by the sword.
12-19.desc: Holy Martyrs Eutychius and Thessalonica, with two hundred men and seventy women.
12-19.greek: Ευτύχιος, Θεσσαλονίκη και οι συν αυτοίς
12-19.name: Eutychius, Thessalonica and companions

12-19.bio: Gregentios was a bishop of the sixth century sent to the land of the Himyarites in southern Arabia after the martyrdom of the Christians of Najran. Tradition relates that he restored the churches, gave laws to the Christian kingdom, and held a famous disputation with the Jew Herban. He reposed in peace.
12-19.desc: Gregentios, Bishop of the Himyarites in Arabia and Ethiopia.
12-19.name: Gregentios of Ethiopia

12-19.bio: Venerable Elias of Murom was, according to tradition, the mighty warrior of the Russian epics who at the end of his life became a monk of the Kiev Caves Lavra in the twelfth century. His relics rest in the Near Caves, and he is honoured as a wonderworker.
12-19.desc: Venerable Elias of Murom, wonderworker of the Kiev Near Caves.
12-19.name: Elias of Murom

12-2.bio:
The holy prophet Habakkuk is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament. Troubled by the prosperity of the wicked, he questioned God and stood upon his watch to await the answer, receiving the word that the righteous shall live by his faith. His prayer, the canticle beginning Lord, I have heard Thy report and was afraid, is sung in the Church as one of the biblical odes of matins.

The Church honors him as a prophet who foresaw the coming of the Lord for the salvation of His people. He is commemorated on December 2.
12-2.name: Habakkuk the Prophet

12-2.bio:
The holy martyr Myrope was born in Ephesus and lived on the island of Chios in the third century, where she devoted herself to prayer and to anointing the tombs of the martyrs with myrrh, from which she took her name. When the soldier Isidore was martyred on Chios, she secretly took his body and buried it with honour.

When the guards were threatened with death for the missing body, Myrope came forward and confessed what she had done. She was scourged and thrown into prison, where tradition relates that she gave up her soul amid a heavenly light and the fragrance of myrrh.
12-2.desc: Holy Martyr Myrope of Chios, who buried the martyr Isidore.
12-2.name: Myrope of Chios

12-2.bio:
Venerable Porphyrios was born in Evia in 1906 and as a boy fled to the Holy Mountain, where he lived in obedience at Kavsokalyvia and received, according to his own account, the gift of spiritual insight. Illness forced him to return to the world, and for many years he served as a priest at a hospital chapel in the heart of Athens, receiving countless people in confession.

Known for his gentleness, his love of the Church's services, and his discernment, he returned to Kavsokalyvia at the end of his life and reposed there on 2 December 1991. He was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2013.
12-2.desc: Venerable Porphyrios of Kavsokalyvia, the clairvoyant elder of Athens (1906-1991).
12-2.name: Porphyrios of Kavsokalyvia

12-2.bio: Solomon was Archbishop of Ephesus, the ancient see of the Apostle John. The Synaxarion records that he governed his church in piety and reposed in peace.
12-2.desc: Solomon, Archbishop of Ephesus, who reposed in peace.
12-2.name: Solomon of Ephesus

12-2.bio:
These four venerable hermits lived in the Egyptian desert in the fourth century. Tradition relates that they were found by the monk Paphnutius, who recorded how they had left the world together as young men and lived for many decades in the wilderness, nourished by God and praying without ceasing.

They reposed in peace in the desert, leaving to the Church the memory of their perfect renunciation.
12-2.desc: Venerable hermits John, Heraclemon, Andrew and Theophilus of the Egyptian desert.
12-2.name: John, Heraclemon, Andrew and Theophilus of Egypt

12-2.bio:
Venerable Cyril was born in the village of Philea in Thrace in the eleventh century. Though married, he lived a life of great austerity, working as a sailor and later withdrawing to a life of prayer near his home, where a small community gathered around him.

Tradition relates that the emperor Alexios Komnenos visited him for counsel. He reposed in peace in the early twelfth century.
12-2.desc: Venerable Cyril Phileotes, ascetic of Thrace and counsellor of emperors.
12-2.name: Cyril Phileotes

12-2.bio: Venerable Athanasius was a monk of the Kiev Caves Lavra in the twelfth century. Tradition relates that after a long illness he died and lay unburied for two days, and then rose again to the astonishment of the brethren, answering all their questions only with the words 'Repent'. He then shut himself in a cave, where he lived in silence and prayer for many years until his repose.
12-2.desc: Venerable Athanasius the Recluse of the Near Caves of Kiev.
12-2.name: Athanasius the Recluse of the Kiev Caves

12-20.bio:
The holy hieromartyr Ignatius the God-Bearer was Bishop of Antioch in the generation after the Apostles, a disciple of the apostolic age who shepherded one of the great churches of the early world. Condemned under the emperor Trajan, he was taken in bonds to Rome, and on the journey wrote seven epistles that remain among the treasures of the early Church, begging the faithful not to hinder his martyrdom; he was given to the wild beasts in the arena.

He called himself the wheat of God, ground by the teeth of beasts to become pure bread of Christ. He is commemorated on December 20.
12-20.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Ignatius the God-Bearer of Antioch.
12-20.name: Ignatius the God-Bearer

12-20.bio: Philogonius was a married lawyer of Antioch who was chosen bishop of the city for his holiness in the early fourth century. He suffered in the last persecutions, stood against the beginnings of the Arian heresy, and reposed in peace in 324. St. John Chrysostom delivered a homily in his honour.
12-20.desc: Philogonius, Bishop of Antioch, praised by Saint John Chrysostom.
12-20.name: Philogonius of Antioch

12-20.bio: The new martyr John was a young tailor from the island of Thasos working in Constantinople. Falsely accused before the Turkish authorities, he refused to embrace Islam and was beheaded in 1652.
12-20.desc: New Martyr John the Tailor of Thasos, martyred in Constantinople.
12-20.name: John the Tailor of Thasos

12-20.bio:
Righteous John of Kronstadt was a Russian parish priest who served for more than fifty years at the cathedral of Kronstadt near St. Petersburg. Celebrating the Divine Liturgy daily, he was famed throughout Russia for his prayer, his charity to the poor, and the healings worked through him.

Author of the spiritual diary 'My Life in Christ', he reposed on 20 December 1908 and was glorified by the Church of Russia.
12-20.desc: Righteous John of Kronstadt, wonderworker and pastor.
12-20.name: John of Kronstadt

12-20.bio: Venerable Ignatius was archimandrite of the Kiev Caves Lavra in the fifteenth century. Known for his prayer and for the healings granted through the Holy Gifts he offered, he reposed in peace, and his relics rest in the Far Caves.
12-20.desc: Venerable Ignatius, Archimandrite of the Kiev Caves Lavra.
12-20.name: Ignatius of the Kiev Caves

12-21.bio:
The holy martyr Juliana was a young Christian of Nicomedia who suffered in the persecutions at the beginning of the fourth century. Betrothed to a pagan of rank, she refused to marry him unless he came to Christ, and for her confession she endured imprisonment and cruel tortures with unshaken constancy before being put to death by the sword.

Her courage moved many who witnessed her sufferings to believe, and the Church honors her among the brave virgin martyrs of Nicomedia. She is commemorated on December 21.
12-21.name: Juliana of Nicomedia

12-21.bio:
The holy martyr Themistocles was a shepherd of Myra in Lycia who suffered under the persecution of Decius in the third century. Tradition relates that when soldiers searched for a Christian named Dioscorides, Themistocles refused to betray him and declared himself a Christian instead.

He was cruelly tortured and beheaded, and is honoured as a martyr of Lycia.
12-21.desc: Holy Martyr Themistocles of Myra in Lycia.
12-21.name: Themistocles of Myra

12-21.bio: These holy martyrs were witnesses of the sufferings of St. Juliana of Nicomedia. Seeing her endurance, five hundred men and one hundred thirty women confessed Christ and were beheaded together with her.
12-21.desc: The five hundred men and one hundred thirty women martyred at Nicomedia with Saint Juliana.
12-21.greek: Πεντακόσιοι Μάρτυρες και Εκατόν Τριάντα Γυναίκες
12-21.name: Five Hundred Martyrs and One Hundred Thirty Women of Nicomedia

12-21.bio: Peter was a monk and iconographer of Volhynia who was made Metropolitan of Kiev and All Russia in the early fourteenth century. He transferred his residence to the rising city of Moscow, where he founded the cathedral of the Dormition, and reposed in peace in 1326. He is honoured as one of the great wonderworkers of Moscow.
12-21.desc: Peter the Wonderworker, Metropolitan of Kiev and All Russia, first hierarch of Moscow.
12-21.name: Peter of Moscow

12-22.bio:
The great martyr Anastasia was a Roman Christian of noble birth who suffered under the persecution of Diocletian at the turn of the fourth century. She devoted her wealth and freedom to visiting imprisoned Christians, tending their wounds and strengthening them for their contest, until she herself was seized and, after many trials, put to death.

She is called Pharmakolytria, Deliverer from Potions, for the faithful seek her protection against poisons, spells, and every harmful thing. She is commemorated on December 22.
12-22.desc: Great Martyr Anastasia the Deliverer from Potions.
12-22.name: Anastasia the Pharmakolytria

12-22.bio: The holy martyr Chrysogonus was a Christian of Rome who instructed St. Anastasia in the faith. Imprisoned under Diocletian, he was taken to Aquileia and beheaded for his confession of Christ.
12-22.desc: Holy Martyr Chrysogonus, teacher of the Great Martyr Anastasia.
12-22.name: Chrysogonus the Martyr

12-22.bio: The holy martyr Theodote was a widow of Nicaea and a companion of St. Anastasia in the persecution of Diocletian. Refusing to deny Christ or to marry a pagan, she was burned to death together with her three young children.
12-22.desc: Holy Martyr Theodote of Nicaea and her three children.
12-22.name: Theodote and her Three Children

12-22.bio: The holy martyr Zoilus is remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day. Tradition records that he confessed Christ and was perfected in peace.
12-22.name: Zoilus the Martyr

12-22.bio: The holy martyr Ischyrion and his companions are commemorated on this day. Tradition relates that Ischyrion was an Egyptian who refused to sacrifice to idols and was put to death for Christ together with those who confessed with him.
12-22.desc: Holy Martyr Ischyrion and those with him.
12-22.name: Ischyrion and companions

12-23.bio:
The Ten Holy Martyrs of Crete suffered together under the persecution of the emperor Decius in the third century. Drawn from various towns of the island, they were brought before the governor at Gortyna, and when they refused to sacrifice to the idols they endured mockery and torments for many days before being beheaded, going to their death rejoicing.

They are the boast of the Church of Crete, which honors them as its own firstfruits among the martyrs. They are commemorated on December 23.
12-23.desc: The Ten Holy Martyrs of Crete.
12-23.name: Ten Martyrs of Crete

12-23.bio: Venerable Nahum was a disciple of Sts. Cyril and Methodius and a fellow-labourer of St. Clement of Ochrid in the enlightenment of the Slavs. He founded the monastery on the southern shore of Lake Ochrid that bears his name, where he reposed in peace in the early tenth century. His relics are venerated there as a source of healing.
12-23.desc: Venerable Nahum the God-bearer, Wonderworker of Ochrid, disciple of Saints Cyril and Methodius.
12-23.name: Nahum of Ochrid

12-23.bio: Niphon was born in Paphlagonia and lived a dissolute youth in Constantinople before coming to deep repentance. Tradition relates that he was later made Bishop of Constantia in Cyprus, where he shepherded his flock in humility and reposed in peace in the fourth century.
12-23.desc: Niphon, Bishop of Constantia in Cyprus.
12-23.name: Niphon of Constantia

12-23.bio: Paul was Bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus in the fourth century. Under the emperor Licinius his hands were burned with hot iron for his confession of Christ, and he bore the marks of his suffering when he took part in the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea. He reposed in peace.
12-23.desc: Paul the Confessor, Bishop of Neocaesarea.
12-23.name: Paul of Neocaesarea

12-23.bio: On this day the Church remembers the consecration of the Great Church of the Holy Wisdom of God in Constantinople, built by the emperor Justinian in the sixth century. For nearly a thousand years it was the cathedral of the Ecumenical Patriarchate and the greatest church of the Christian world.
12-23.desc: Commemoration of the consecration of the Great Church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.
12-23.name: Dedication of Hagia Sophia

12-24.bio:
The holy virgin martyr Eugenia was the daughter of a distinguished Roman family in the third century. Coming to faith in Christ, according to tradition she fled a life of privilege, entered monastic life disguised as a man, and became known for holiness and healing; after many trials, in which her identity and her innocence were revealed, she returned to Rome and was put to death for the faith in the persecutions of that age.

Her feast falls on the eve of the Nativity, joining her witness to the light of the coming feast. She is commemorated on December 24.
12-24.desc: Holy Virgin-martyr Eugenia of Rome, on the Eve of the Nativity.
12-24.name: Eugenia of Rome

12-24.bio: The holy martyr Philip was the father of St. Eugenia and governor of Egypt under the Roman emperors. Brought to faith through his daughter, tradition relates that he was made Bishop of Alexandria and was slain for Christ.
12-24.desc: Holy Martyr Philip, father of Saint Eugenia.
12-24.name: Philip the Martyr

12-24.bio: The new martyr Ahmed was a Turkish official in Constantinople in the seventeenth century. Tradition relates that, attending the Divine Liturgy, he saw a light descend upon the Christians, and was baptised in secret. When he openly confessed Christ before his fellow officials he was beheaded in 1682.
12-24.desc: New Martyr Ahmed the Calfa of Constantinople, a convert from Islam.
12-24.name: Ahmed the Calfa

12-24.bio: The holy virgin martyr Basilla was a noble maiden of Rome who was brought to faith by St. Eugenia. Refusing marriage for the sake of Christ, she was slain by the sword.
12-24.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Basilla, companion of Saint Eugenia.
12-24.name: Basilla the Martyr

12-24.bio: The holy martyrs Protas and Hyacinth were servants of St. Eugenia who followed her into the monastic life and shared her confession of Christ. They were beheaded at Rome.
12-24.desc: Holy Martyrs Protas and Hyacinth, servants of Saint Eugenia.
12-24.name: Protas and Hyacinth

12-24.bio: Venerable Nicholas was a soldier of the Byzantine army in the ninth century. Tradition relates that, having resisted temptation on the eve of a battle, he was shown in a vision that he alone of his company would be spared, and in thanksgiving he left the army and became a monk, living in repentance until his repose.
12-24.desc: Venerable Nicholas the former soldier, monk of Bulgaria.
12-24.name: Nicholas the Monk

12-24.bio: Venerable Antiochus was a monk of the Lavra of St. Sabas in the seventh century. After the Persian invasion of Palestine he composed the Pandects, a compendium of Scripture and the Fathers for the use of monks, and reposed in peace.
12-24.desc: Venerable Antiochus of the Lavra of Saint Sabas, author of the Pandects.
12-24.name: Antiochus the Monk

12-25.bio:
The Nativity of our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus Christ, kept on December 25, celebrates the birth in the flesh of the Son of God from the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem. Laid in a manger because there was no room at the inn, the newborn King was glorified by angels, worshipped by shepherds, and honored with gifts by Magi from the East.

Christmas is, after Pascha, the greatest feast of the church year, prepared by a forty-day fast. In the Child of Bethlehem the Church confesses God become man, that man might be brought back to God.
12-25.desc: The Nativity of our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus Christ.
12-25.name: Nativity of Christ

12-25.bio: On the day of the Nativity the Church also remembers the Magi from the East who, led by the star, came to Bethlehem and offered the newborn King gold, frankincense and myrrh. Warned in a dream, they returned to their own country by another way.
12-25.desc: The Adoration of the Magi who came from the East to worship the newborn Christ.
12-25.name: Adoration of the Magi

12-25.bio: The Church remembers the shepherds who were keeping watch over their flocks by night when the angel announced to them the birth of the Saviour. They came in haste to Bethlehem, found the Child lying in the manger, and returned glorifying God.
12-25.desc: Commemoration of the shepherds who saw the Lord in Bethlehem.
12-25.name: Shepherds of Bethlehem

12-26.bio:
On the day after the Nativity of Christ, the Church gathers in synaxis to honor the Most Holy Theotokos, from whom the Saviour was born in the flesh. Having celebrated the birth of the Lord, the faithful turn with gratitude to His Mother, through whose obedience the Incarnation came to pass.

This is among the most ancient feasts of the Mother of God, and it follows a pattern kept throughout the church year, in which the day after a Great Feast honors the principal servant of the mystery. The synaxis proclaims Mary truly Theotokos, the Birth-giver of God.
12-26.desc: Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos — day after Nativity.
12-26.name: Synaxis of the Theotokos

12-26.bio:
On the Sunday after the Nativity the Church keeps the synaxis of three holy kinsmen of the Lord according to the flesh: David the Prophet and King, from whose line the Messiah was born; Joseph the Betrothed, the righteous elder who guarded the Virgin and the Christ Child and led them to safety in Egypt; and James the Brother of the Lord, first Bishop of Jerusalem.

The feast honors those bound most closely to the mystery of the Incarnation by kinship and faithful service. It is kept on the Sunday after the Nativity, commemorated in this calendar on December 26.
12-26.desc: Sunday after Nativity — Synaxis of Joseph, David the Prophet, and James.
12-26.name: King David, Joseph, James

12-26.bio: The hieromartyr Euthymius was Bishop of Sardis in the eighth and ninth centuries and a steadfast defender of the holy icons. Exiled repeatedly under the iconoclast emperors, he was scourged so cruelly in the reign of Theophilos that he died of his wounds in 831.
12-26.desc: Hieromartyr Euthymius the Confessor, Bishop of Sardis.
12-26.name: Euthymius of Sardis

12-26.bio: On the day after the Nativity the Church remembers how Joseph, warned by an angel, took the Child and His Mother and fled into Egypt from the wrath of Herod, and remained there until the death of the king, that the word of the prophet might be fulfilled: Out of Egypt have I called My Son.
12-26.desc: The flight of the Holy Family into Egypt.
12-26.name: Flight into Egypt

12-26.bio: Venerable Constantine was born to a Jewish family of Synnada in Phrygia in the ninth century and came to faith in Christ, receiving baptism and becoming a monk on Mount Olympus in Bithynia. Tradition relates that he travelled to Cyprus and other places, working miracles, and reposed in peace.
12-26.desc: Venerable Constantine of Synnada, a convert from Judaism.
12-26.name: Constantine the Jew

12-26.bio: Venerable Evarestus was born in Galatia in the ninth century and became a monk of the Studion monastery in Constantinople, where he lived in strict asceticism and reposed in peace.
12-26.desc: Venerable Evarestus of the Monastery of Studion.
12-26.name: Evarestus of Studion

12-26.bio: The new martyr Constantius was a Russian hieromonk of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos who served as a chaplain in Constantinople. Tradition relates that he fell into apostasy, repented bitterly on the Holy Mountain, and returned to Constantinople to confess Christ, where he was beheaded in 1743.
12-26.desc: New Hieromartyr Constantius the Russian of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos.
12-26.name: Constantius the Russian

12-26.bio: Venerable Nikodemos was a monk of Mount Athos of Serbian origin who in the fourteenth century founded the monasteries of Vodita and Tismana in Wallachia, establishing organised monastic life in the Romanian lands. He reposed in peace in 1406 and is honoured by the Church of Romania.
12-26.desc: Venerable Nikodemos the Sanctified of Tismana, founder of monasteries in Romania.
12-26.name: Nikodemos of Tismana

12-27.bio:
St. Stephen, the Protomartyr and Archdeacon, was one of the seven deacons chosen by the Apostles to serve the first church in Jerusalem. Full of grace and power, he preached Christ boldly; accused before the council, he beheld the heavens opened and the Son of Man at the right hand of God, and was stoned to death, praying for his slayers, while the young Saul, the future Apostle Paul, stood by.

He is the first martyr of the Church, and his witness became the pattern for all martyrs after him. His feast is kept on December 27, within the days of the Nativity.
12-27.name: Stephen the First Martyr

12-27.bio: Venerable Theodore was a monk of the Lavra of St. Sabas who, with his brother Theophanes, was sent to Constantinople to defend the holy icons. Under the emperor Theophilos the brothers were beaten and had verses branded on their faces, whence their name Graptoi, the Branded. Theodore died in exile around 840.
12-27.desc: Venerable Theodore the Branded, Confessor of the holy icons.
12-27.name: Theodore Graptus

12-27.bio: Theodore was Patriarch of Constantinople in the seventh century, in the days of the emperor Constantine IV. He governed the Church with piety and reposed in peace.
12-27.name: Theodore of Constantinople

12-27.bio: Venerable Luke was a monk and abbot of Triglia on the coast of Bithynia. The Synaxarion records that he laboured in asceticism and reposed in peace.
12-27.desc: Venerable Luke of Triglia in Bithynia.
12-27.name: Luke of Triglia

12-27.bio: The holy martyr Mauricius was an officer at Apamea in Syria who, with seventy soldiers under him, confessed Christ before the emperor Maximian. His son Photinus was beheaded before his eyes; tradition relates that Mauricius and the others were then smeared with honey and left bound in a marsh, where they died of the stings of insects.
12-27.desc: Holy Martyrs Mauricius, his son Photinus, and the seventy soldiers martyred at Apamea.
12-27.name: Mauricius and the Seventy Martyrs

12-28.bio:
The Twenty Thousand Holy Martyrs of Nicomedia suffered at the beginning of the fourth century, in the great persecution under the emperors Diocletian and Maximian. According to tradition, a vast multitude of Christians had gathered in the church of Nicomedia for the feast of the Nativity when the building was surrounded; commanded to sacrifice to the idols, they refused as one, and the church was set alight, the faithful within perishing in the flames with prayer on their lips.

The Church honors them as a whole congregation crowned together. They are commemorated on December 28.
12-28.desc: The Twenty Thousand Holy Martyrs of Nicomedia.
12-28.name: Twenty Thousand Martyrs of Nicomedia

12-28.bio: These holy martyrs suffered at Nicomedia in the great persecution of Diocletian, together with the multitude of Christians burned in the church of the city. Several of them, including Gorgonius, Peter and Dorotheus, were officials of the imperial palace who confessed Christ openly; the priest Glycerius, the deacon Migdonius and the eunuch Indes were put to death with them in various ways.
12-28.desc: Holy Martyrs Indes, Gorgonius, Peter, Zeno, Dorotheus, Mardonius, Glycerius, Migdonius and Theophilus of Nicomedia.
12-28.greek: Ίνδης, Γοργόνιος, Πέτρος, Ζήνων, Δωρόθεος, Μαρδόνιος
12-28.name: Indes, Gorgonius and the Martyrs of Nicomedia

12-28.bio: The holy martyr Domna was a pagan priestess of the imperial palace at Nicomedia who came to faith in Christ through reading the Scriptures. Escaping the palace, she lived for a time in a monastery and among the Christians of the city, and after the burning of the church she was seized and beheaded.
12-28.desc: Holy Martyr Domna of Nicomedia, a former pagan priestess.
12-28.name: Domna of Nicomedia

12-28.bio:
Venerable Simon was a hermit of Mount Athos in the thirteenth century. Tradition relates that he saw a star shining night after night above a great rock and, understanding it as a sign, founded upon it the monastery of the Nativity of Christ, now called Simonopetra.

After his repose his relics gave forth myrrh, and he is honoured as the founder and protector of the monastery.
12-28.desc: Venerable Simon the Myrrh-gusher, founder of the Monastery of Simonopetra on Mount Athos.
12-28.name: Simon the Myrrh-gusher

12-28.bio: The holy martyr Secundus is remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day. Tradition records that he confessed Christ and was perfected by the sword.
12-28.name: Secundus the Martyr

12-28.bio: Venerable Ignatius was a Russian monk of the sixteenth century who founded a hermitage at Loma in the region of Yaroslavl, where he lived in poverty and prayer. He reposed in peace in 1591.
12-28.desc: Venerable Ignatius of Loma and Yaroslavl.
12-28.name: Ignatius of Loma

12-29.bio:
The Holy Innocents are the young children of Bethlehem and its borders slain by King Herod, who, fearing the newborn King announced by the Magi, ordered the death of all the male children of two years and under. The Gospel sees in their death the fulfillment of the prophecy of Rachel weeping for her children, and the Church numbers them by tradition at fourteen thousand.

They are honored as the first blood shed for Christ, infants crowned as martyrs before they could speak. They are commemorated on December 29.
12-29.desc: The 14,000 Holy Innocents slain by Herod in Bethlehem.
12-29.name: Holy Innocents of Bethlehem

12-29.bio: Venerable Marcellus was born in Apamea in Syria in the fifth century and became a monk of the monastery of the Akoimetoi, the Unsleeping Ones, near Constantinople, where the praise of God was sung without ceasing day and night. Chosen abbot, he governed the brotherhood with wisdom and took part in the struggles of the Church for the Orthodox faith. He reposed in peace.
12-29.desc: Venerable Marcellus, Abbot of the Monastery of the Unsleeping Ones.
12-29.name: Marcellus of the Unsleeping Ones

12-29.bio: George was a cleric of the Great Church of Constantinople in the ninth century and a friend of St. Photios, and was later made Bishop of Nicomedia. He is remembered as a composer of canons and hymns still sung in the services of the Church, and reposed in peace.
12-29.name: George of Nicomedia

12-29.bio: Venerable Thaddeus was a monk of the Studion monastery in the time of St. Theodore the Studite. For refusing to trample on an icon of Christ at the command of the iconoclast emperor Leo the Armenian he was beaten so severely that he died of his wounds a few days later, in the early ninth century.
12-29.desc: Venerable Thaddeus the Confessor of the Monastery of Studion.
12-29.name: Thaddeus of Studion

12-29.bio: On this day, alongside the Holy Innocents, the Church remembers all Christians who through the ages have given their lives for the glory of Christ by hunger, thirst, freezing and the sword, whose names are known to God alone.
12-29.desc: Commemoration of all Orthodox Christians who died as martyrs for Christ by hunger, thirst, cold and the sword.
12-29.greek: Πάντες οι Χριστιανοί οι μαρτυρικώς τελειωθέντες
12-29.name: All Christians Martyred by Hunger, Cold and the Sword

12-3.bio:
The holy prophet Zephaniah, one of the twelve minor prophets, prophesied in the kingdom of Judah in the days of King Josiah, before the Babylonian captivity. He proclaimed the great day of the Lord, calling the people to seek righteousness and humility, and he foretold that a meek and lowly remnant would trust in the name of the Lord and rejoice in His salvation.

The Church honors him among the prophets whose words point ahead to the joy of the Messiah's coming. He is commemorated on December 3.
12-3.name: Zephaniah the Prophet

12-3.bio:
Venerable Theodoulos was a patrician and eparch of Constantinople in the days of the emperor Theodosius the Great. After the death of his wife he gave away his possessions and left the city, and tradition relates that he took his stand upon a pillar near Edessa, where he lived in prayer and fasting for many years until his peaceful repose.

The Greek Synaxarion also remembers on this day Theodoulos of Cyprus, the fool for Christ.
12-3.desc: Venerable Theodoulos, former eparch of Constantinople, who became a stylite.
12-3.name: Theodoulos the Eparch

12-3.bio: The hieromartyr Theodore was Archbishop of Alexandria in the early centuries of the Church. Tradition relates that the pagans of the city seized him, crowned him with thorns, and dragged him through the streets before he was beheaded for his confession of Christ.
12-3.name: Theodore of Alexandria

12-3.bio:
Venerable John was born in Nicopolis of Armenia in the fifth century and while still young was made Bishop of Colonia. Longing for stillness, he secretly left his see and came to Palestine, where he entered the Great Lavra of St. Sabas as an unknown novice.

When his rank was at last discovered, he withdrew into solitude, living as a recluse in his cell for many decades. He reposed in peace at a great age in the sixth century.
12-3.desc: Venerable John the Silent, Bishop of Colonia, monk of the Lavra of Saint Sabas.
12-3.name: John the Hesychast

12-3.bio: The new martyr Angelis was a physician from Argos in the Peloponnese who settled on the island of Chios. Tradition relates that after an unguarded word was taken by the Turks as a profession of Islam, he refused to deny Christ and was beheaded at Chios in 1813, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
12-3.desc: New Martyr Angelis, physician of Argos, martyred at Chios.
12-3.name: Angelis of Argos

12-3.bio: The hieromartyr Gabriel served as Patriarch of Constantinople in the seventeenth century. Tradition relates that he was accused before the Ottoman authorities of baptising a Muslim and, refusing to save his life by denying Christ, was hanged at Bursa in 1659.
12-3.desc: Hieromartyr Gabriel, Patriarch of Constantinople, put to death by the Ottomans.
12-3.name: Gabriel Patriarch of Constantinople

12-3.bio: Venerable George was born in Transylvania in the eighteenth century and became a disciple of St. Paisius Velichkovsky on Mount Athos and in Moldavia. He was sent to restore the abandoned monastery of Cernica near Bucharest, where he gathered a large brotherhood and established the hesychast tradition of his teacher. He reposed in peace in 1806 and is honoured by the Church of Romania.
12-3.desc: Venerable George of Cernica, restorer of monastic life in Romania.
12-3.name: George of Cernica

12-30.bio:
The holy virgin martyr Anysia was a young Christian of Thessaloniki who lived at the turn of the fourth century, in the days of the persecution under Diocletian. Left wealthy by her parents, she gave her goods to the poor and lived in prayer and quietness. On her way to the gathering of the faithful she was stopped by a soldier who tried to drag her to a pagan sacrifice; when she confessed Christ and resisted, he ran her through with his sword.

She is honored as one of the beloved martyrs of Thessaloniki. She is commemorated on December 30.
12-30.name: Anysia of Thessaloniki

12-30.bio:
The new martyr Gideon was born in Thessaly in the eighteenth century. As a boy he was forced into Islam, but he escaped and became a monk of the monastery of Karakalou on Mount Athos, where he lived for many years in repentance.

Returning to Thessaly to confess Christ, he was tortured and put to death at Tyrnavos in 1818.
12-30.desc: New Monk-martyr Gideon of Karakalou, martyred at Tyrnavos.
12-30.name: Gideon of Karakalou

12-30.bio: Venerable Theodora was the daughter of a noble family of Caesarea in Cappadocia in the eighth century. Dedicated to God from childhood, she was taken from the monastery to be married by imperial command, but tradition relates that she escaped and returned to the convent, where she lived in asceticism until her peaceful repose.
12-30.desc: Venerable Theodora of Caesarea in Cappadocia.
12-30.name: Theodora of Caesarea

12-30.bio: Anysios was Bishop of Thessalonica at the turn of the fifth century, the successor of Ascholius and a friend of St. Ambrose of Milan and St. John Chrysostom, whom he supported in his troubles. He governed his church with wisdom and reposed in peace.
12-30.name: Anysios of Thessalonica

12-30.bio: The holy martyr Philetairos was a Christian of Nicomedia who confessed Christ under Diocletian. Tradition relates that he endured many tortures and exile, and that he brought others to faith before his death.
12-30.name: Philetairos of Nicomedia

12-30.bio: Venerable Leo the Archimandrite is remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day as a monastic father who governed his brotherhood in holiness and reposed in peace.
12-30.name: Leo the Archimandrite

12-30.bio: Macarius was Metropolitan of Moscow in the sixteenth century, in the reign of Ivan the Terrible. He gathered the lives of the saints and the writings of the Fathers into the Great Menaion, presided over the councils that glorified many Russian saints, and reposed in peace in 1563.
12-30.desc: Macarius, Metropolitan of Moscow and All Russia, compiler of the Great Menaion.
12-30.name: Macarius of Moscow

12-31.bio:
St. Melania was a Roman noblewoman of one of the wealthiest families of the empire who, in the era of the great flowering of monasticism, renounced rank and riches for the sake of Christ. She gave her vast possessions to the poor and to the churches, freed those enslaved to her household, and devoted herself to asceticism, prayer, and the service of the monks and holy places of the East, ending her days in the Holy Land.

She is honored as a model of voluntary poverty embraced out of love for God. She is commemorated on December 31.
12-31.desc: Venerable Melania the Elder of Rome.
12-31.name: Melania the Elder

12-31.bio: The holy martyr Zoticus was a priest of Constantinople in the fourth century who used his wealth and the emperor's gifts to build a home for orphans and for lepers, whom he cared for with his own hands. Tradition relates that the emperor Constantius, angered at his charity, had him dragged to death behind mules.
12-31.desc: Holy Martyr Zoticus the Priest, keeper of orphans and lepers in Constantinople.
12-31.name: Zoticus the Orphan-keeper

12-31.bio: Theophylact was born at Euripos in Euboea in the eleventh century and served as a deacon and teacher in Constantinople before being made Archbishop of Ochrid and All Bulgaria. He is remembered above all for his commentaries on the Gospels and Epistles, which follow the teaching of St. John Chrysostom and are still widely read. He reposed in peace in the early twelfth century.
12-31.desc: Theophylact of Euripos, Archbishop of Ochrid and All Bulgaria, commentator on the Scriptures.
12-31.name: Theophylact of Ochrid

12-31.bio: Venerable Gelasius is remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day as an ascetic who reposed in peace; the Church also remembers on this day the venerable Gaius.
12-31.name: Gelasius the Venerable

12-31.bio: The Ten Holy Virgins are remembered together on this day. The Synaxarion records that they confessed Christ and were perfected by the sword.
12-31.name: Ten Holy Virgins

12-31.bio: The holy martyr Olympiodora is remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day. Tradition records that she confessed Christ and was perfected by fire.
12-31.name: Olympiodora the Martyr

12-4.bio:
St. Barbara the Great Martyr lived in the late third century. According to tradition, she was the daughter of a wealthy pagan, Dioskoros, who confined her in a tower; coming to faith in Christ, she confessed Him openly, and after cruel tortures she was put to death by her own father, upon whom judgment swiftly fell.

She is invoked as a protector against sudden and unprepared death, and by long tradition is the patroness of those who work with fire and explosives, including miners and artillerymen. Her feast on December 4 is a beloved name day for Barbara and Varvara.
12-4.desc: Great Martyr Barbara of Heliopolis, patron against sudden death.
12-4.name: Barbara the Great Martyr

12-4.bio:
Venerable John was born in Damascus in the seventh century to a Christian family in the service of the caliph. Leaving the world, he became a monk of the Lavra of St. Sabas near Jerusalem, where he wrote his great works in defence of the holy icons and his summary of the Orthodox faith.

He is also one of the Church's greatest hymnographers, author of the Paschal canon and of many hymns still sung today. He reposed in peace in the eighth century.
12-4.desc: Venerable John of Damascus, theologian, hymnographer and defender of the holy icons.
12-4.name: John of Damascus

12-4.bio:
The hieromartyr Seraphim was born in Thessaly and became a monk and later abbot of a monastery near Agrafa before being made Archbishop of Phanarion and Neochorion. When an uprising against the Ottomans failed in 1601, he was seized though he had no part in it, and was tortured and put to death for refusing to deny Christ.

He is greatly honoured in Thessaly, where his relics are venerated.
12-4.desc: Hieromartyr Seraphim, Archbishop of Phanarion and Neochorion in Thessaly.
12-4.name: Seraphim of Phanarion

12-4.bio: The holy martyr Juliana was a Christian woman of Heliopolis who witnessed the sufferings of the great martyr Barbara. Moved by her courage, she openly confessed Christ and was seized and tormented together with her, and the two were beheaded on the same day.
12-4.desc: Holy Martyr Juliana, who suffered together with Saint Barbara.
12-4.name: Juliana of Heliopolis

12-4.bio: John was Bishop of Polybotum in Phrygia in the eighth century, in the days of the iconoclast emperor Leo the Isaurian. He boldly confessed the veneration of the holy icons and was renowned as a wonderworker both during his life and after his repose.
12-4.desc: John the Wonderworker, Bishop of Polybotum in Phrygia, confessor of the holy icons.
12-4.name: John of Polybotum

12-4.bio: The holy martyrs Christodoulos and Christodouli the Virgin are remembered by the Greek Synaxarion on this day. Tradition records that they confessed Christ and were perfected by the sword.
12-4.desc: Holy Martyrs Christodoulos and Christodouli the Virgin.
12-4.name: Christodoulos and Christodouli

12-5.bio:
Venerable Savvas the Sanctified, born in Cappadocia in the fifth century, entered the monastic life as a boy and became one of the great fathers of the Judean desert. He founded the Great Lavra near Jerusalem, which bears his name to this day, and gathered thousands of monks under his guidance, while defending the Orthodox faith of the Council of Chalcedon.

The liturgical order long followed throughout the Orthodox Church, the Typikon of St. Savvas, is linked to his monastery. He reposed in peace in old age and is commemorated on December 5.
12-5.desc: Venerable Sabas the Sanctified, founder of the Great Lavra near Jerusalem.
12-5.name: Savvas the Sanctified

12-5.bio: The holy martyr Diogenes confessed Christ before the pagans and, according to the Synaxarion, was perfected by stoning. His name is kept on this day in the Greek calendar.
12-5.desc: Holy Martyr Diogenes, who was stoned for Christ.
12-5.name: Diogenes the Martyr

12-5.bio: The holy martyr Anastasius was a cloth-fuller of Salona in Dalmatia in the time of Diocletian. Tradition relates that he painted a cross on the door of his workshop, and when he refused to deny Christ, he was drowned in the sea with a stone tied to his neck.
12-5.desc: Holy Martyr Anastasius the Fuller of Salona in Dalmatia.
12-5.name: Anastasius the Fuller

12-5.bio: Venerable Nektarios was born in Bitola and came to the Holy Mountain, where he lived in obedience to the elder Philotheos at a cell in Karyes. He was known for his humility and unceasing prayer, and reposed in peace around the year 1500; his relics are venerated on Athos.
12-5.desc: Venerable Nektarios of Bitola, ascetic of Karyes on Mount Athos.
12-5.name: Nektarios the Athonite

12-5.bio: Venerable Philotheos was a hesychast of Karyes on the Holy Mountain in the fifteenth century, the spiritual father of St. Nektarios of Bitola. He lived in stillness and prayer at his cell and reposed in peace.
12-5.desc: Venerable Philotheos, hesychast of Karyes on Mount Athos.
12-5.name: Philotheos of Karyes

12-5.bio: Cosmas was Protos of the Holy Mountain in the thirteenth century, when the emperor Michael Palaiologos sought to impose union with Rome. Refusing to accept the union, he was hanged at Karyes and many monks of the cells were slain with him. The Holy Mountain honours them as martyrs for the Orthodox faith.
12-5.desc: Cosmas the Protos of the Holy Mountain and the monks of Karyes martyred by the Latinizers.
12-5.name: Cosmas the Protos and the Martyrs of Karyes

12-6.bio:
St. Nicholas the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Myra in Lycia, lived in the fourth century and is one of the most beloved saints of the Church. Renowned for secret almsgiving — according to tradition he saved three daughters of a poor man from ruin by gifts of gold given at night — he was a defender of the innocent and of the true faith in the age of the First Ecumenical Council.

He is the patron of sailors and travelers, of children, and of countless churches and towns across the Orthodox world, and his relics rest in Bari in Italy. His feast is kept on December 6.
12-6.desc: Archbishop of Myra in Lycia, the Wonderworker, patron of sailors, children, and travellers.
12-6.name: Nicholas the Wonderworker

12-6.bio: The new martyr Nicholas Karamanos was a Christian of Smyrna who, according to tradition, was accused before the Turkish authorities and pressed to embrace Islam. He held fast to Christ and was hanged in Smyrna in 1657.
12-6.desc: New Martyr Nicholas Karamanos of Smyrna.
12-6.name: Nicholas Karamanos

12-6.bio: Venerable Antony was born in the region of Novgorod in the fifteenth century and, after the death of his wife, became a monk. He founded a monastery on the river Siya in the far north of Russia, where he laboured in great austerity and was known as a wonderworker. He reposed in peace in 1556.
12-6.desc: Venerable Antony of Siya, founder of a monastery in the Russian north.
12-6.name: Antony of Siya

12-6.bio: Venerable Nilus was a Russian hermit of the sixteenth century who lived alone on the island of Stolobny in Lake Seliger. Tradition relates that he never lay down to sleep, resting only on hooks fixed to the wall of his cell. He reposed in peace in 1554, and a great monastery later arose at the place of his labours.
12-6.desc: Venerable Nilus, hermit of Stolobny island on Lake Seliger.
12-6.name: Nilus of Stolbensk

12-7.bio:
St. Ambrose was Archbishop of Milan in the fourth century and one of the great Fathers of the Western Church. Governor of the region when a disputed episcopal election threatened the city with strife, he was acclaimed bishop by the people while still a catechumen; he gave his wealth to the poor, defended the Nicene faith against Arianism, and did not fear to call even emperors to repentance. His preaching helped bring Blessed Augustine to conversion.

A teacher and hymnographer whose writings nourished East and West alike, he reposed in peace. He is commemorated on December 7.
12-7.desc: Archbishop of Milan, one of the four great Latin Fathers.
12-7.name: Ambrose of Milan

12-7.bio: The holy martyr Athenodorus was a monk of Mesopotamia who suffered under the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that he endured many tortures, and that when the executioner raised the sword against him he fell dead, so that the saint gave up his soul in prayer, untouched by the blade.
12-7.name: Athenodorus of Mesopotamia

12-7.bio: Venerable Gerasimos came from Euripos, the region of Chalkis in Euboea, and embraced the monastic life. The Greek Synaxarion records that he laboured in asceticism and reposed in peace.
12-7.desc: Venerable Gerasimos from Euripos in Euboea.
12-7.name: Gerasimos of Euripos

12-7.bio: Venerable Gregory was a hesychast of the fourteenth century, a disciple of the Sinaite tradition of prayer, who founded the monastery on the south-west coast of Mount Athos that bears his name. He is honoured by the brotherhood of Grigoriou as its founder and heavenly patron.
12-7.desc: Venerable Gregory, founder of the Monastery of Grigoriou on Mount Athos.
12-7.name: Gregory of Grigoriou

12-7.bio: Holy Philothea was born in Tarnovo in the thirteenth century. From childhood she gave food to the poor, and tradition relates that her father, angered at her charity, struck her and she died. Her relics were later brought to Curtea de Arges in Wallachia, where she is venerated as a protectress of the Romanian people.
12-7.desc: Holy Philothea of Thrace, protectress of Romania.
12-7.name: Philothea of Arges

12-7.bio: Venerable Ammoun was an Egyptian of the fourth century who, married against his will, persuaded his wife to live with him in chastity and later withdrew to the desert of Nitria, where he became the father of a great multitude of monks. A friend of St. Anthony the Great, he reposed in peace; tradition relates that Anthony saw his soul carried up to heaven.
12-7.desc: Venerable Ammoun, founder of monastic life in the desert of Nitria.
12-7.name: Ammoun of Nitria

12-7.bio: Venerable Paul is remembered for his perfect monastic obedience. Tradition relates that at his elder's command he thrust his hand into a burning furnace and was unharmed, and that he reposed in peace after a life of humility.
12-7.name: Paul the Obedient

12-8.bio:
Venerable Patapios was born in Thebes of Egypt and embraced the ascetic life in the desert from his youth. Fleeing the fame that his holiness drew, he came to Constantinople, where he lived in stillness and prayer, and many were healed through his intercession; the Church's hymns remember him especially as a healer of the sick.

His relics are treasured at the monastery that bears his name near Loutraki in Greece, where the faithful come in great numbers to venerate him. He is commemorated on December 8.
12-8.name: Patapios

12-8.bio:
These holy apostles of the Seventy are named in the New Testament as fellow-workers of St. Paul. Sosthenes is mentioned at the head of the First Epistle to the Corinthians; Apollos was the eloquent Alexandrian who watered what Paul had planted; Tychicus carried Paul's letters to the churches; Epaphroditus brought the gifts of the Philippians to Paul in prison.

Tradition relates that each became a bishop and laboured in the preaching of the Gospel.
12-8.desc: Holy Apostles of the Seventy Sosthenes, Apollos, Cephas, Tychicus, Caesar and Epaphroditus.
12-8.greek: Σωσθένης, Απολλώς, Κηφάς, Τυχικός, Καίσαρ και Επαφρόδιτος
12-8.name: Apostles Sosthenes, Apollos, Cephas, Tychicus, Caesar and Epaphroditus

12-8.bio: Sophronios was born in Cyprus and, after a life of piety and learning, was made Archbishop of the island. The Synaxarion records that he shepherded his flock with wisdom and reposed in peace.
12-8.name: Sophronios of Cyprus

12-8.bio: Venerable Parthenios was a monk of Chios in the nineteenth century, a hymnographer and iconographer who founded the monastery of Panagia Voithia near the town of Chios. He reposed in peace in 1883 and is honoured by the faithful of the island.
12-8.desc: Venerable Parthenios of Chios, founder of the Monastery of Panagia Voithia.
12-8.name: Parthenios of Chios

12-9.bio:
On December 9 the Church commemorates the conception of the Most Holy Theotokos by the righteous Anna. Childless for many years, Joachim and Anna prayed with tears, and according to tradition an angel announced to each of them that God would grant them a child who would be spoken of in all the world. Anna conceived and bore Mary, the future Mother of God.

The feast celebrates the power of God who looses barrenness, and honors the holy ancestors of Christ. It stands within the Nativity Fast as a quiet foreshadowing of the salvation prepared for the human race.
12-9.desc: Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos by the Righteous Anna.
12-9.name: Conception of the Theotokos by Anne

12-9.bio: Righteous Hannah was the wife of Elkanah and for many years was childless. Praying in tears at the sanctuary of Shiloh, she vowed to give her son to the Lord, and God granted her the prophet Samuel, whom she brought to serve before the Ark. Her song of thanksgiving is sung by the Church as the third ode of the canon.
12-9.desc: Righteous Hannah the Prophetess, mother of the Prophet Samuel.
12-9.name: Hannah the Prophetess

12-9.bio: Venerable Stephen, called the New Light, was a monk of Constantinople in the tenth century. Tradition relates that he lived in extreme asceticism, enclosed in a narrow cell near the church of St. Antipas, taking almost no food, and that he reposed in peace after many years of such labour.
12-9.desc: Venerable Stephen the New Light of Constantinople.
12-9.name: Stephen the New Light

12-9.bio: The holy martyrs Narses, Isaac and Sositheus are remembered together on this day. Narses suffered in Persia for refusing to worship the sun; tradition records that all three confessed Christ and were perfected by the sword.
12-9.desc: Holy Martyrs Narses the Persian, Isaac and Sositheus.
12-9.name: Narses, Isaac and Sositheus
